justification.rationale: The adapter use is the only supported way to ship a Node production build, and ssg: null is the sanctioned option satisfying a hard spec constraint; no other API choice is gratuitous or novelty-driven.

findings.issue: nodeServerAdapter is labeled 'alpha preview' in Qwik's API reference (https://qwik.dev/api/qwik-city-vite-node-server/), so its shape could change without a semver-major signal.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep — it's the standard 'qwik add node-server' output — but track the adapter's option surface when upgrading @builder.io/qwik-city, and pin the version (already done) so a patch release can't silently change behavior.

findings.issue: Exact (unranged) pin to @builder.io/qwik 1.20.3, a patch release published days before this review (2026-10-25).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for reproducibility, but it also means you absorb the newest patch immediately and get no automatic fixes. Consider '~1.20.3' with a lockfile, or a brief note explaining the pin.

summary: The app is firmly on the stable Qwik 1.x API surface with no experimental flags, no unstable_* names, and none of the v2-RC packages. The only preview-documented API is the nodeServerAdapter in one generated adapter config file, where it's the only supported path for a Node production build and its ssg: null option is required by the spec's no-build-time-data rule. Experimental risk is very low and fully contained.
